title: Contextual Log Router with Graphable Session Traces and Otel Handoff
creator: Liam Patel
description: Goal: Replace brittle, per-source routing rules with a schema-aware contextual router that builds a lightweight session graph for each request envelope, attaches standardized correlation context, and emits enriched structured logs to both Loki (label-first) and Elasticsearch (field-first) sinks.
acceptance_criteria: Edge-side telemetry envelopes can be processed and assigned a session_id and span_links within 50ms median processing time
Router enriches events with correlation_context (trace_id, session_id, user_id if present) and emits to Loki with stable labels: tenant, service, session_id
Events destined for ES include normalized fields (tenant, service, trace_id, http_status, error_code) and pass schema validation against the ingest registry
Backpressure and DLQ behavior: when downstream is overloaded, router triggers tenant-aware shedding and writes to DLQ with reason codes
Otel trace handoff: for any log bearing trace_id, the router attaches span_link(s) and calls trace-handoff hook (idempotent retry) documented in design doc
End-to-end test coverage (integration) demonstrating correlation across logs -> traces -> Grafana dashboard panels for latency and error aggregation
progress_updates: 2025-03-01 - Triage complete. Spike planned to validate session-graph approach and Loki label cardinality trade-offs.
2025-03-03 - Spike implemented: in-memory session graph PoC using ring buffer per-tenant. Measured median processing time 32ms with synthetic load (1k RPS).
2025-03-06 - Design review with Platform and SRE. Decided to limit session graph retention to 60s by default and expose policy per-customer to avoid high cardinality.
2025-03-08 - Implemented schema registry adapter and a transformation pipeline that can emit both label-first (Loki) and field-first (ES) representations from same canonical event.
2025-03-10 - Integrated OTEL span_link generation. Need to finalize retry semantics for trace-handoff hook (at-most-once vs at-least-once); SRE prefers at-most-once with compensating logs.

2025-03-12 - First end-to-end staging run succeeded for 200 RPS. Observed label explosion when user_id is present in 30% of events; added heuristic to promote user_id to label only when <5k unique values per 10m window.
notes: Trade-offs considered: storing full session state vs lightweight recent span pointers. We chose lightweight pointers to keep memory O(active sessions) and avoid cross-tenant leak risks.
Loki vs ES mapping: labels kept minimal (tenant, service, session_id) and high-cardinality fields (user_id, request_id) are moved to fields with controlled promotion heuristics.
Backpressure strategy: tenant-priority queue + probabilistic shedding + DLQ. Will coordinate with billing to surface shed events when customers hit throughput limits.
Observability: Added internal metrics: router.process_ms histogram, sessions.active_gauge, label_promotion_rate, dlq_write_count. Dashboards PR pending.
Open question: whether the trace-handoff should live in the router process or a separate async worker. Current PoC keeps it inline for simplicity; may move to worker for better isolation.
next_steps: Finalize trace-handoff retry policy with SRE and Security (expected decision by 2025-03-15)
Add integration tests that demonstrate correlation across log -> trace -> metric workflows and update runbook
Instrument promotion heuristics and tune defaults based on staging traffic for two weeks
Submit dashboards PR to observability repo and schedule demo with Product and SRE
review_feedback: 2025-03-06 - SRE (Hannah Lee): prefer at-most-once trace-handoff and emit compensating log when handoff fails. Also requested metric for handoff_failure_count.
2025-03-09 - Platform (Anders Nylund): ensure tenant-affinity routing keys are cryptographically stable so we can shard downstream storage efficiently.
2025-03-11 - Security (Nadia Ruiz): requested threat model doc for DLQ contents and KMS requirement for persisted DLQ data.
